description.fun: Axew's tusks break easily, but they grow back fast, and harder and sharper each time. It uses them to crush hard berries, to gash trees and boulders to mark its territory, and to play by knocking tusks with other Axew. In ancient times people used its shed tusks as cooking knives. Peculiar tooth marks on a boulder or tree mean an Axew is probably living nearby.
description.guide: Axew is a Dragon-type Pokémon with axe-like tusks that regrow harder each time they break. It lives in nests in the ground. It evolves into Fraxure, then Haxorus.
description.tagline: A little dragon whose broken tusks grow back stronger.

description.fun: Unlike Axew's, Fraxure's tusks never grow back once they break, so after every battle it carefully sharpens them on river rocks, and it won't use them unless it truly has to. Its skin is as hard as a suit of armour. Turf fights between Fraxure are fierce, and it clashes with Bisharp over the best sharpening stones. It neatly cuts its prey into two portions: one to eat now, one for later.
description.guide: Fraxure is the evolved form of Axew, a Dragon-type Pokémon whose tusks can shatter rock but don't grow back once broken. It is fiercely territorial. It evolves into Haxorus.
description.tagline: A careful dragon that sharpens tusks it can't replace.

description.fun: Haxorus's axe-blade tusks are its pride and joy: they stay sharp even after slicing through steel beams, and it licks up dirt to take in the minerals that keep them in top shape. It's usually kind-hearted, but touch its tusks and it becomes incredibly angry. Haxorus was the very first Pokémon designed for Black and White, drawn while Platinum was still in development, and Axew and Fraxure were designed later from it.
description.guide: Haxorus is the final form of Axew, a Dragon-type Pokémon with huge, axe-like tusks that can cut steel. It is usually gentle but very territorial.
description.tagline: A kind-hearted dragon with tusks that cut through steel.
